headline_marked: 12 [[Bangladeshis killed in Middle East conflict]], says Minister
headline: 12 Bangladeshis killed in Middle East conflict, says Minister
summary: Expatriates' Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury reveals death tolls and repatriation efforts in Parliament.
details: Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury informed Parliament today that 12 Bangladeshis have died in the recent Middle East war.
The deceased include five people in Lebanon, three in Saudi Arabia, two in the United Arab Emirates, and one each in Iraq and Bahrain.

Of the 12, nine bodies were repatriated to Bangladesh, while one was buried in the respective country. Families of the repatriated received Tk 35,000 for burial expenses and Tk 50,000 in special financial assistance.
The government also financed the repatriation of 186 people from Iran, including 12 women and eight children, amid the ongoing conflict.
In a separate update, the minister stated that four Bangladeshis who traveled to Russia in April have died after reports emerged they were being forcibly sent into the war.
To mitigate risks from Middle East instability, the government is working to expand employment opportunities in Thailand, South Korea, Japan, and Malaysia.
The minister noted that between 2004 and June 2026, approximately 10.91 million Bangladeshis went to Middle Eastern countries for employment, though exact current numbers are difficult to determine.
caption:
12 Bangladeshis have died in the Middle East conflict, according to the Expatriates' Welfare Minister.

Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury informed Parliament today that 12 Bangladeshis have died in the recent Middle East war.

The deceased include five people in Lebanon, three in Saudi Arabia, two in the United Arab Emirates, and one each in Iraq and Bahrain.

Of the 12, nine bodies were repatriated to Bangladesh, while one was buried in the respective country. Families of the repatriated received Tk 35,000 for burial expenses and Tk 50,000 in special financial assistance.

The government also financed the repatriation of 186 people from Iran, including 12 women and eight children, amid the ongoing conflict.

In a separate update, the minister stated that four Bangladeshis who traveled to Russia in April have died after reports emerged they were being forcibly sent into the war.

To mitigate risks from Middle East instability, the government is working to expand employment opportunities in Thailand, South Korea, Japan, and Malaysia.

The minister noted that between 2004 and June 2026, approximately 10.91 million Bangladeshis went to Middle Eastern countries for employment, though exact current numbers are difficult to determine.

headline: 50,000 hotel bookings cancelled in Cox’s Bazar due to flood fears
summary: Tourism owns in ownersyndicateate that fear of flooding has led to huge losses for the local hospitality industry.
details: Approximately 50,000 hotel bookings have been cancelled in Cox's Bazar, the primary tourism hub of Bangladesh.
The mass cancellations are attributed to flood fears among tourists, causing a significant financial blow to hotel owners and local businesses.
The hospitality sector in the city is currently facing a severe downturn as visitors avoid the trip during thele flood-prone season.
Local authorities and business owners are hoping for a weather forecast that encourages tourists to return to the beach town.
